summary: rebrowser-playwright is a drop-in replacement for Playwright that applies the rebrowser-patches to evade automation detection. The core mechanism patches out the `Runtime.enable` CDP command leak — a well-known fingerprint used by Cloudflare, DataDome, and other anti-bot systems. It works by intercepting Playwright's internal CDP session initialization and replacing the automatic `Runtime.enable` call with custom context-creation strategies: (1) `addBinding` mode (default) creates a random-named binding to capture the main-world execution context ID without ever sending `Runtime.enable`; (2) `alwaysIsolated` runs all scripts in an isolated world; (3) `enableDisable` briefly enables then disables Runtime. The patches also mask the utility world name (`__playwright_utility_world__` → configurable generic name) and sourceURL (`pptr://...` → `app.js`). Only Chromium is supported; Firefox and WebKit are explicitly unpatched. The package is a thin wrapper that simply re-exports `rebrowser-playwright-core` (the actual patched core), with version numbers tracking upstream Playwright releases.

apiSurface:
- Identical to Playwright API: `import { chromium, firefox, webkit } from 'rebrowser-playwright'` or `require('rebrowser-playwright')`
- No new programmatic APIs — configuration entirely via environment variables:
  - `REBROWSER_PATCHES_RUNTIME_FIX_MODE`: 'addBinding' | 'alwaysIsolated' | 'enableDisable' | '0'
  - `REBROWSER_PATCHES_UTILITY_WORLD_NAME`: string | '0' to disable
  - `REBROWSER_PATCHES_SOURCE_URL`: string | '0' to disable
  - `REBROWSER_PATCHES_DEBUG`: '1' for verbose logging
- Added `browser._connection()` method for direct CDP access (not in upstream)
- CLI: `npx playwright` (same as upstream via cli.js)
- Installation: `npm i rebrowser-playwright` then `npx playwright install`
integrationPoints:
- Drop-in replacement: change `playwright` → `rebrowser-playwright` in package.json (or use npm alias: `playwright: npm:rebrowser-playwright@^1.52.0`)
- Works with existing Playwright test runner, fixtures, selectors, tracing
- Compatible with playwright-extra via `addExtra(rebrowserPlaywrightCore)` pattern (documented for puppeteer, same concept)
- Queue/pipeline integration: standard Playwright browser launch/connect APIs work unchanged
- Proxy support: uses Playwright's native proxy config (no custom proxy handling)
- Search/matching: page.evaluate, page.route, page.waitForSelector all functional; isolated world mode may affect main-world variable access
- Cloudflare/DataDome bypass: primary value prop — passes rebrowser-bot-detector tests
- CI/CD: same as Playwright (GitHub Actions, Docker images available via upstream)
strengthsForVeridian:
- Zero code changes required for existing Playwright scrapers — true drop-in
- Addresses the single most impactful automation fingerprint (Runtime.enable) used by major anti-bot vendors
- Actively maintained with rapid version tracking (Playwright 1.52.0 released April 2025, patched May 2025)
- Environment-variable config enables A/B testing patched vs unpatched in same codebase
- Debug mode helps diagnose context creation issues
- Open-source patches (MIT) with transparent implementation
- Works with Playwright's full feature set: tracing, screenshots, network interception, multiple contexts
- rebrowser-patches has strong community validation (1.4k stars, cited by patchright, puppeteer-real-browser)
weaknessesForVeridian:
- Chromium-only: Firefox and WebKit patches explicitly not implemented — limits browser diversity for fingerprinting
- Single maintainer with commercial cloud-service upsell (Rebrowser.net) — sustainability risk if business pivots
- Patches are inherently fragile: tied to Playwright internals (crConnection, crPage, frames.ts) that change frequently
- Known breakage: `page.pause()` broken with fix enabled (debugging workflow disrupted)
- Isolated world mode breaks main-world access — may require code changes for complex page interactions
- No TypeScript types beyond upstream (re-exports playwright-core types)
- Wrapper repo low adoption (58 stars) vs patches repo — limited real-world battle testing visibility
- Must re-run patcher after every `npm install` unless using pre-patched npm packages
- No built-in fingerprint randomization (canvas, WebGL, navigator) — requires separate solution
limitations: Seeded from prior analysis; maturity signals may be approximate
